anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet (mcu.kicad_sch, pages 1/4 and 2/4) the USB-C receptacle VBUS pin A4 is wired to BOTH the +5V power symbol and the global label 'VBUS'. The 'VBUS' label is the post-mux rail on the Power sheet (power.kicad_sch, page 4/4): U5 pin 1 (OUT) → VBUS → U8 pin 3 (IN). The +5V label is the mux input: U5 pin 2 (IN2) → +5V. As drawn, the USB 5V input net and the mux output / buck input net are merged into one.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, the USB VBUS pins belong to the +5V net that feeds U5 IN2, while VBUS is the mux output net and is 'distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux'. The USB connector pins should carry only +5V, never VBUS.

evidence.quote: J12 (USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_14P) VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) → +5V net → U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2).

a single OUT (pins 1/1_1/8/8_1) onto the VBUS net (the board's internal, unregulated/pre-buck rail — note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux).
mcu.kicad_sch (page 1/4): J12 pin A4 row shows the +5V power arrow and the global label 'VBUS' on the same wire; power.kicad_sch (page 4/4): U5 pin 1 OUT → VBUS, U5 pin 2 IN2 → +5V.

anomalies.impact: Shorting +5V (mux IN2) to VBUS (mux OUT / buck IN) defeats the TPS2121 power-mux arbitration: the two input rails and the output are tied together, so the seamless switchover cannot function. With the 12 V barrel jack connected the mux would drive ~12 V onto VBUS, which is hard-tied to the USB-C VBUS pin, back-feeding 12 V into the host/USB port and into the buck input, instead of the intended muxed rail.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the specification (power mux, buck, heater high-side switch, three MAX31855 channels, WS2812, fan clamps all wired as described), but the USB-C VBUS pin is labeled with both +5V and VBUS, merging the 5 V input rail with the post-mux VBUS rail — a deviation from the spec's stated separation of those two nets.
